steps.body: In the ordered set 2, 5, 8, the first number is least and the last number is greatest.
steps.narration: In the ordered set 2, 5, 8, the first number is least and the last number is greatest.

widget.prompt: What number comes right before 14? Hop one back and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 14 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop back to reach 13.
12 goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 1 hop back from 14 to reach 13.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 back from 14: you land on 13.
widget.successFeedback: 13 — one hop back, and one hop earlier in the song always means less.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — one hop back from 14 reaches 13.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right before 14 means a single hop back, stopping on 13.

predict.reveal: The greatest is whichever the counting song reaches last, and the least whichever it reaches first; written order is irrelevant.

cml.actionGoal: Pair the groups one to one, or place both numbers in the counting song, for kcm greatest least.
invariants: Comparison rests on two facts that never move: pairing one to one leaves the bigger group with leftovers, and a number later in the counting song always names more — which is what kcm greatest least uses.
misconceptions: Judging by how much space a group fills, by the size of the things in it, or by which number was written first.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more joined the smaller group, would the pairing come out even?

widget.prompt: Three numbers: 4, 9, 2. How do you find the greatest?

options.label: The first one written — here 4
options.feedback: Written order is arbitrary; the counting song's order is what compares them.

options.label: The one written biggest on the page
options.feedback: Ink size is not amount; a tiny 9 still beats a giant 4.

options.label: Add them all together
options.feedback: Adding builds a new number; comparing only asks which existing one is latest.

options.label: The one latest in the counting song — here 9
options.feedback: Correct — later in the song means more, so the greatest is the one the count reaches last.

widget.prompt: Start at 16 and hop back four times. Tap the least landing reached.

commonLandings.feedback: That is the starting number. Complete all 4 hops.
That is one hop beyond 12. Stop after exactly 4 hops.

widget.successFeedback: 12 — the complete hop path lands on the requested smaller number.
widget.lowFeedback: Check the start, direction, and number of hops before choosing the landing.

misorderFeedback.feedback: 7 before 4 starts with the greatest value. Counting order begins with the smallest value, 4.
5 cannot come before 4 — the smaller number always stands earlier in counting order.

widget.missFeedback: Find the smallest value first, then place each next-greater number after it.

widget.prompt: There are 7 stars and 6 hearts. Which statement is true?

options.label: They are equal
options.feedback: Equal needs the pairing to come out even; here one side is left holding extras (7 against 6).

options.label: More stars
options.feedback: Correct — 7 stars against 6 hearts; pairing one to one leaves stars unmatched.

options.label: More hearts
options.feedback: Pairing one to one uses every heart with stars to spare, so the hearts are not the larger group.

options.label: You cannot tell
options.feedback: You can always tell — pair the groups one to one and look at which side has leftovers.
